disease_label_per_paper: Primary HIV infection presenting as mononucleosis-like syndrome and acute aseptic meningoencephalitis
presentation_summary: 47-year-old woman admitted with 10 days of fever 38-39 C, headache, diffuse myoarthralgias of arms and legs, and photophobia.
History included unprotected sex with an HIV-seropositive regular sexual partner during the preceding year.
Exam showed fever with chills, moderate-to-severe headache, mild neck rigidity, generalized lymphadenopathy, and splenomegaly.
Labs showed WBC 12.7 x10^9/L with lymphomonocyte predominance 70% and 12% atypical lymphocytes; liver and renal function were normal.
Chest radiograph was normal; abdominal ultrasound showed homogeneous splenomegaly.
Brain MRI showed contrast enhancement of meninges; CSF showed protein 0.85 g/L and 35 cells/mm3 with 100% mononuclear cells.

HIV rapid ELISA and p24 antigen were positive, Western blot was indeterminate with p24 band, plasma HIV RNA was 1,980,000 copies/mL, CSF HIV RNA was 150,000 copies/mL, and later ELISA/WB confirmed seroconversion.
